ml-tree-split-07: Sirf ek node ki impurity chahiye, aur 'entropy using $\log_2$' likha hai — Gini nahi, natural log nahi.
$H = -p\log_2 p - (1-p)\log_2(1-p)$ with $p = 7/10$; dono classes ka term lena hai.
Pehla term: $-0.7\log_2 0.7 \approx 0.360$. Ab $-0.3\log_2 0.3$ nikaalo aur jodo. Trap: $\ln$ use kiya toh value chhoti aayegi.
ml-tree-split-08: CART Gini impurity maangta hai: class fractions ke squares se banta hai, log nahi lagta.
$p_A = 0.75$ toh $p_A^2 = 0.5625$; $p_B^2$ bhi nikaalo. Trap: sirf $\sum p_i^2$ likh ke ruk mat jao — 1 se minus karna hai.
ml-tree-split-09: Classes 4 hain, 2 nahi — 'binary max 1 bit' wala rule yahan seedha nahi lagta.
Ek class ka term: $-\frac14\log_2\frac14 = \frac14 \times 2$. Ab chaaron jodo. Trap: har term ko $p_i$ se multiply karna mat bhoolo.
ml-tree-split-10: Parent 8:4 hai, balanced nahi — iski entropy 1 nahi hogi. Teen children hain, sizes 6, 5, 1.
Green aur blue pure hain toh unki entropy 0; red $3{:}3$ ki entropy 1. Ab parent $H(2/3)$ nikaalo. Trap: children ko $1/3$-$1/3$ weight mat do.
ml-tree-split-11: Split P ka ek child pure hai lekin usme sirf 1 example hai — dekho weight kitna milega.
Har split ke liye $\frac{n_L}{20}G_L + \frac{n_R}{20}G_R$ nikaalo; jiska chhota, wo chuna jaata hai.
Q: $8{:}2$ child ka Gini $= 1 - 0.8^2 - 0.2^2 = 0.32$, dono children same. Ab P ka right child $9{:}10$ ka Gini nikaalo. Trap: simple average mat lo.
ml-tree-split-12: Har statement ek alag measure check karta hai — gain, Gini, entropy, misclassification. Ek-ek ko chhote calculation se parkho.
Rules: Gini $= 1 - \sum p_i^2$; $H = -\sum p_i\log_2 p_i$ with $0\log 0 = 0$; misclassification $= 1 - \max p_i$.
Teesra option: $p = 0$ wali class ka term $0$ hai, toh asal mein kitni classes bachi? Chautha: $1 - \max(0.7, 0.3)$ nikaalo aur 0.42 se milao.
ml-tree-split-13: Har threshold data ko left ($x \le t$) aur right mein todta hai. Sirf ek child pure hona kaafi nahi — dono children ka weighted impurity dekho.
Parent $4{:}4$ hai toh $H = 1$. Gain $= 1 - \frac{n_L}{8}H_L - \frac{n_R}{8}H_R$; chaaron $t$ ke liye counts likho.
$t = 2.5$: left $2{:}0$ (H = 0), right $2{:}4$ (H $\approx 0.918$), gain $= 1 - \frac68(0.918)$. Baaki teen thresholds isi tarah karo. Trap: equal-size children wala split automatically best nahi.
ml-tree-split-14: Counts 6, 3, 1 hain — teen classes. Binary wale limits (entropy max 1, Gini max 0.5) yahan automatically nahi lagte.
Fractions $0.6, 0.3, 0.1$. Gini $= 1 - \sum p_i^2$; $H = -\sum p_i\log_2 p_i$; misclassification $= 1 - \max p_i$.
$\sum p_i^2 = 0.36 + 0.09 + 0.01$ — isse pehla option check karo. Entropy ka pehla term $-0.6\log_2 0.6 \approx 0.442$; baaki do jodo aur 1 se compare karo.
ml-tree-split-15: P mein 4 examples, Q mein 80 — lekin dono mein classes ka ratio dekho.
$H = -\sum p_i\log_2 p_i$ sirf fractions $p_i$ par depend karta hai, total count $n$ par nahi.
P ke liye $p_+ = 2/4$, Q ke liye $p_+ = 40/80$. Dono fractions compare karo. Trap: 0.5 Gini ki value hai, entropy ki nahi.
ml-tree-split-16: Parent mein teen classes barabar hain — iski entropy 1 bit nahi, usse zyada hogi.
Parent $= \log_2 3 \approx 1.585$. Left child mein sirf A aur B barabar hain, toh uski $H$ binary $50{:}50$ jaisi. Trap: left child ka $8/12$ weight mat bhoolo.
ml-bias-variance-06: Total error diya hai aur variance poocha hai — decomposition ko ulta use karna hai. Dhyan: noise ka SD diya hai, variance nahi.
bias$^2 = 0.09$ aur $\sigma^2 = 0.16$. Ab dono ko 0.50 se ghatao. Trap: 0.3 ya 0.4 ko bina square kiye mat ghatao.
ml-bias-variance-07: Training error 1% aur validation 30% — itna bada gap kis problem ka signal hai: bias ya variance?
Rule: low train + high validation = overfit (high variance). Variance ghatane ke liye model ki flexibility kam karo.
Har option ke liye poocho: ye tree ko zyada flexible banata hai ya kam? Trap: training error aur ghatane se validation error nahi sudhrta.
ml-bias-variance-08: 6 se divide karne par $T$ biased ho jaata hai. MSE ke do hisse hain — dono nikaalne padenge.
$E[T] = 50/6 \approx 8.333$, toh bias $\approx -1.667$; ise square karo. Ab $\mathrm{Var}(T) = 5 \times 20/36$ nikaalo. Trap: bias ko bina square kiye mat jodo.
ml-bias-variance-09: Har option ek alag cheez pe hai: noise, bagging, 1-NN, aur zyada data. Har ek ke liye socho bias badalta hai ya variance.
Decomposition: error $=$ bias$^2$ + variance + $\sigma^2$. Averaging aur zyada data variance ghataate hain; model ka galat shape bias banata hai.
1-NN ka training error 0 hota hai — wo flexible hai ya rigid? Seedhi line ko parabola ke data par fit karo: lakhon points ke baad bhi curve pakdegi?
ml-bias-variance-10: $k = n$ ka matlab: har prediction ke liye saare training points neighbours ban jaate hain.
k-NN regression prediction $=$ $k$ nearest targets ka average. $k = n$ par ye average har $x$ ke liye same hoga.
Prediction har jagah $\bar y$ — ab socho ye constant model data ka pattern pakadta hai (bias) aur training set badalne par kitna hilta hai (variance).
ml-bias-variance-11: Chaar predictions ka spread variance deta hai, aur unka average true value 4 se kitna door hai wo bias deta hai.
bias $= \overline{\hat f} - 4$; variance $= \frac14\sum(\hat f_i - \overline{\hat f})^2$. Dono ko (bias squared karke) jodo.
$\overline{\hat f} = (6 + 4 + 7 + 7)/4 = 6$, toh bias $= 2$. Ab deviations $0, -2, 1, 1$ se variance nikaalo. Trap: divisor 4 hai, 3 nahi.
ml-bias-variance-12: Table mein training MSE lagatar gir raha hai, validation MSE pehle girta phir badhta hai — U-shape pehchano.
Model selection validation error se hota hai. High train + high val = bias; low train + high val = variance.
Validation row mein sabse chhoti value dhoondo. Phir degree 1 ka gap (21.0 − 20.1) aur degree 8 ka gap (37.5 − 1.2) compare karo.
ml-bias-variance-13: Average lene se fluctuations cancel hote hain. 'Independent' word important hai — covariance terms zero.
Sum ka variance $= 5 \times 0.2 = 1.0$. Ab constant $\frac15$ bahar nikalne par kis power se divide hoga? Trap: $\sqrt 5$ se divide karna SD ka rule hai.
ml-bias-variance-14: $\lambda$ badhana = weights ko zyada shrink karna = model ko kam flexible banana. Har option isi direction se judge karo.
Kam flexibility: bias ↑, variance ↓. $\lambda = 0$ least squares hai jo training MSE ka minimum deta hai.
Pehla option: kya koi penalty wala fit training data pe least squares se behtar ho sakta hai? Chautha: 'every increase' — bahut bade $\lambda$ par model kya predict karega?
ml-bias-variance-15: Model bilkul sahi $f$ jaanta hai, toh bias aur variance dono zero. Phir bhi naye $y$ mein kuch bacha hai — kya?
Error $= y - f(x) = \varepsilon$, toh expected squared error $= E[\varepsilon^2] = \sigma^2$.
Stem mein SD diya hai: $\sigma = 0.5$. Ise variance mein badlo. Trap: SD ko seedha error mat likho.
ml-bias-variance-16: Dono curves 18–19 par mil ke flat ho gaye hain, jabki doosra model 5 la raha hai. Gap chhota hai ya level ooncha?
Small gap + high error = high bias (underfit). Big gap = high variance. Zyada data sirf gap band karta hai, plateau neeche nahi laata.
Gap $= 19 - 18 = 1$ hai — variance ka problem lagta hai? Ab chautha option: agar noise variance 18 hota toh boosted model 5 kaise laata?
ml-cv-06: Pehle ginno kitne alag candidates hain (har kernel–$C$ pair ek candidate), phir har candidate kitni baar train hota hai.
Fits $=$ (number of folds) $\times$ (number of candidates); refit sirf tab jodo jab stem bole.
Candidates $= 2 \times 5$, not $2 + 5$. Ab ise folds se multiply karo. Trap: final refit yahan nahi ginna.
ml-cv-07: Har model ek fold ko validation ke liye chhodta hai — baaki pe train hota hai. Fold ka size pehle nikaalo.
Ek fold $= 200/8 = 25$ points. Ab socho kitne folds training mein jaate hain. Trap: 25 validation fold hai, training nahi.
ml-cv-08: LOOCV mein har point ko hata ke baaki 6 mein se nearest neighbour dhoondhna hai — point khud apna neighbour nahi ban sakta.
Har point ke liye Manhattan distance $|\Delta x_1| + |\Delta x_2|$ baaki points tak nikaalo; nearest ki class predict hogi. Error rate $=$ galat$/7$.
P3 $(0,3)$: P6 tak distance $2$, P1 tak $3$ — toh prediction P6 ki class. Baaki points bhi aise hi check karo. Trap: denominator 7 hai, 6 nahi.
ml-cv-09: Har fold ko predict karte waqt sirf doosre fold ke targets ka mean use hoga — saare chaar ka nahi.
Fold 1 held out: prediction $= \text{mean}\{5, 7\}$. Fold 2 held out: prediction $= \text{mean}\{1, 3\}$. CV MSE $=$ chaaron squared errors ka average.
Fold 1 ke liye prediction $6$, toh errors $(1-6)^2 = 25$ aur $(3-6)^2 = 9$. Ab fold 2 karo. Trap: dono fold MSEs ko jodna nahi, average lena hai.
ml-cv-10: Ek point ka ek hi fold hota hai. Wo fold kitni baar validation banta hai, aur baaki baar point kahan hota hai?
k-fold mein har point exactly ek baar held-out hota hai; baaki $k - 1$ models mein training mein.
$k = 5$: ek model mein point validation mein gaya. Baaki models mein kya? Trap: 'validation count' aur 'training count' alag sawaal hain.
ml-cv-11: Char statements: chhota $k$, $k = n$, shuffling ka asar, aur computation. Har ek ko alag se socho.
k-fold mein $k$ fits per candidate, har fit $\frac{k-1}{k}n$ points par. Folds random assignment se bante hain (LOOCV ko chhod ke).
$k = 2$ par har model $n/2$ pe train hota hai — final model se behtar ya bura? Aur $k$ badhane par fits ki ginti badhti hai ya ghat-ti?
ml-cv-12: Har point ko hata ke baaki teen mein se sabse paas wale $x$ ka $y$ prediction banta hai — point khud ko predict nahi kar sakta.
LOOCV MSE $= \frac14\sum (y_i - y_{\text{nearest other}})^2$; har $x$ ke liye nearest doosra $x$ dhoondo.
$x = 1$ ka nearest $x = 2$ hai, toh prediction 5, error $(3-5)^2 = 4$. Baaki teen bhi karo; $x = 4$ ke liye 2 aur 7 ki distance compare karo. Trap: 4 se divide karo, 3 se nahi.
ml-cv-13: Do loops hain: bahar 5 folds, aur har outer fold ke andar ek poori CV + ek refit. Pehle ek outer fold ka kaam gino.
Ek outer fold $=$ (inner folds $\times$ candidates) $+ 1$ refit. Total $=$ outer folds $\times$ ye count.
Ek outer fold ke andar inner CV fits $= 4 \times 3 = 12$. Ab refit jodo aur 5 outer folds se multiply karo. Trap: full-data fit yahan nahi hai.
ml-cv-14: CV ek model ko ek number deta hai — chaaron folds ko mila ke. Kisi ek fold ki best value se decide mat karo.
CV error $= \frac14(e_1 + e_2 + e_3 + e_4)$ har model ke liye; sabse chhota average select hota hai.
P ka sum $= 0.10 + 0.30 + 0.12 + 0.28 = 0.80$, average 0.20. Ab Q aur R ke averages nikaalo. Trap: R ka 0.05 akela fold hai.
ml-cv-15: Dono $k$ ke liye alag-alag LOOCV error nikaalna hai, phir chhota wala chunna hai. Held-out point apna neighbour nahi ho sakta.
Har $x$ ko hata ke baaki 6 mein se $k$ nearest dhoondo aur majority class se compare karo. Error $=$ galat$/7$.
$k = 1$, $x = 1$: nearest $x = 3$ (class B), asli A — galat. $k = 3$, $x = 1$: neighbours $3, 4, 6$ ki majority dekho. Trap: point ko khud ka neighbour mat gino.
ml-cv-16: Do cheezein alag rakho: validation folds (jo data ko baant-te hain) aur training sets (jo baaki folds se bante hain).
k-fold: data ko $k$ disjoint folds mein baanto; model $i$ fold $i$ pe test, baaki $k - 1$ pe train. Fold models sirf error estimate ke liye.
Teesra option: CV ke baad final model kaise banta hai — average se ya refit se? Chautha: $k = 5$ mein model 1 aur model 2 ke training sets mein kitne folds common hain?
ml-leakage-06: Har step ke liye poocho: kya ye data se kuch 'seekh' raha hai (median, components), aur kis data se?
Leak-free rule: jo bhi fit hota hai (imputer, PCA, scaler) sirf training rows par fit ho; test rows par sirf apply ho.
Step 2 ka median kis set se aaya? Step 3 ka PCA kin rows par fit hua? Trap: test set ko 'chhoona' leak nahi, test se 'seekhna' leak hai.
ml-leakage-07: Prediction discharge ke waqt banana hai. Har feature ke liye socho: kya ye us waqt maloom hota hai?
Target leakage: aisa feature jo outcome ke baad record hota hai, ya sirf positive cases mein hota hai.
Har option ko timeline pe rakho: pichhle 12 months, current stay, age — sab discharge se pehle. Ab 'readmitted ward' kab record hoga?
ml-leakage-08: Group CV mein folds patients ke hisaab se bante hain — ek patient ke saare scans ek hi fold mein.
Patients per fold $= 120/4$; scans per fold $=$ patients per fold $\times$ 6.
Pehle $120/4 = 30$ patients per fold. Ab inke scans gino. Trap: training folds ke scans nahi, sirf validation fold ke.
ml-leakage-09: Har option mein dekho: kya evaluation data (validation fold ya test set) ne training, preprocessing ya tuning ko kahin chhua?
Rule: jo bhi data se seekha jaata hai (oversampling, encoding, tuning) wo sirf training data se ho; test set sirf aakhri report ke liye.
Oversampling poore data par hua toh ek row ki copy kahan-kahan ja sakti hai? Epochs test accuracy dekh ke chune toh wo accuracy fair report hai?
ml-leakage-10: Pehle 24 months sirf training ke liye hain. Kitne months test hone hain aur kitne-kitne ke blocks mein?
Windows $=$ (test months)$/3$; trainings $=$ windows $\times$ models per window.
Test months $25$ se $36$ tak $= 12$ months. Blocks likh ke gino: 25–27, 28–30, … Trap: har window mein 2 models train hote hain.
ml-leakage-11: Labels coin flips hain aur features unse independent — asal mein koi signal hai hi nahi. Toh 85% kahan se aaya?
Feature selection bhi 'training' hai: leak-free CV mein ye har training fold ke andar dobara hona chahiye.
Socho 5,000 random features mein se 50 'sabse correlated' chunne mein kin labels ka use hua — validation folds wale bhi? Naye data pe coin flip ka best guess kitna sahi hoga?
ml-leakage-12: Prediction order place hote waqt banana hai. Har feature ke liye poocho: kya tab tak ye value ban chuki hoti hai?
Leak: jo feature outcome (return) ke baad hi record hota hai, ya sirf returned orders ke liye hota hai.
'Earlier orders' ka return rate past se aata hai. Ab refund amount aur return request ke days — ye kab record hote hain, aur kis order ke liye?
ml-leakage-13: Sales data time-ordered hai. Deployment mein model ke paas sirf past hota hai — evaluation mein bhi wahi hona chahiye.
Rule: har test month se pehle ke months hi training mein hon (train on past, test on future).
Har option ke liye ek test month lo, jaise year 2 ka March, aur dekho kya year 3–5 ke months training mein aa sakte hain.
ml-leakage-14: Leak-free matlab scaler ka mean aur SD sirf training values $2, 4, 6, 8$ se aayenge — test row ka 20 unme shaamil nahi.
Training mean $= 20/4 = 5$; deviations $-3, -1, 1, 3$. Inse population SD nikaalo. Trap: 20 ko mean/SD mein mila diya toh z bahut chhota aayega.
ml-leakage-15: 50 configurations mein se 'best' chuna gaya — jis score se chuna, wahi score report karna fair hai kya?
Unbiased estimate ke liye data aisa ho jisne training ya selection mein koi role na nibhaaya ho.
Socho: agar saari 50 configurations barabar achhi hon, toh unke CV scores ka maximum asli performance se upar hoga ya neeche? Ab har option ka data source dekho.
ml-leakage-16: Imputer bhi data se 'seekhta' hai. Leak-free mein kaun se values uska mean banayengi — test wale 40, 50 bhi?
Fill value $=$ training rows ki observed values ka mean (missing row ko count mein mat gino).
Training observed values: $6, 9, 15$; inka sum $30$. Ab sahi denominator se divide karo. Trap: test values milaane se mean bahut bada ho jaayega.
